title: Template
description: Template defining business logic for transforming events into ledger transfers

$schema.description: Canonical path to the JSON schema that describes this template

template_id.$comment: Must match the code field in legs

event_type.description: Type of event this template processes

description.description: Detailed description of template purpose and behavior
examples: Processes cross-border payments using nostro/vostro accounts with automatic fee calculation

trigger.description: Business event that triggers this template

capabilities.description: Optional capability tags that opt the template into specific behaviours or overrides.
capabilities.$comment: New capabilities can be added via enum expansion without altering the template structure.

mask.description: Glob pattern for valid account codes

description.description: Human-readable description of the account type

from_matched_event.description: Opts this purpose into matched-event account derivation: when the producer does not supply the purpose, event-service resolves it to the unique account of the event named by extra_metadata.matched_event_id whose code matches mask, and rejects the event otherwise. Templates using this flag must declare matched_event_id in metadata_schema and list it in required. Defaults to false.

account_code_validations.description: Validations for account codes by purpose

version.description: Optional explicit version (if omitted, resolve active version). Policy versions are edition years (e.g. 2023) or small revision numbers, so four digits admit every real version; accounting-rule-engine enforces the same 1..9999 bound.

description.description: Human-readable description of the accounting treatment

accounting_treatments.description: Accounting treatment classifications and policy references. A template with no accounting treatment is off balance sheet.

impact.description: Net impact on this account type

ledger_scope.description: Ledger scope identifier this impact applies to. Must match a key in ledger_scope_descriptions.

financial_statements_impact.description: Net accounting impact on financial statements by account type per ledger scope. For templates with capabilities allowing FX or intercompany transfers, each ledger scope must declare impacts for all account types touched by its legs.
financial_statements_impact.$comment: Templates with cross-ledger operations must explicitly declare impacts per scope, including no_impact when debits and credits cancel. Business validation allows at most one declaration for each account type per ledger_scope, so each ledger_scope can have at most six entries.

ledger_scope_descriptions.description: Human-readable descriptions for each ledger scope used by this template. Required when capabilities include FX or intercompany transfers.

^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+)*$.description: Description of how this template uses the referenced ledger scope.

name.description: Variable name used in legs and other expressions

value.description: CEL expression to calculate the variable value

description.description: Human-readable description of what this variable represents
examples: Calculated fee with minimum of 100 minor units

type.description: JSON primitive type of the evaluated variable. Required when export is true: event-service type-checks the evaluated value against it before stamping the exported variable onto the event.

export.description: Exports the evaluated variable onto the accepted event as a platform-derived {name, type, value} entry in exported_variables. Evaluation or type failure rejects the event. Defaults to false.

variables.description: Variables for calculations and business logic. Evaluated sequentially, can reference previous variables.
variables.$comment: Variables contain ALL business logic. Legs only reference variable names.

expression.description: CEL expression that must evaluate to true

description.description: Human-readable description of what this validation ensures

validations.description: Business rule validations that must all pass for the event to be processed

debit_account.description: Reference for the debit account (variable or direct selector)
debit_account.$comment: References an earlier variable or a direct accounts.<purpose> selector

debit_account_type.description: Expected account type for the debit account
debit_account_type.$comment: Runtime validation ensures the actual account matches this type. Prevents business logic errors.

credit_account.description: Reference for the credit account (variable or direct selector)
credit_account.$comment: References an earlier variable or a direct accounts.<purpose> selector

credit_account_type.description: Expected account type for the credit account
credit_account_type.$comment: Runtime validation ensures the actual account matches this type. Accounting equation is preserved.

oneOf.description: Reference for the transfer amount (variable or selector)
Literal integer amount in minor currency units

amount.$comment: Prefer references; literals allowed for fixed adjustments

description.description: Human-readable description of this leg's purpose

ledger_scope.description: Ledger scope identifier for this leg. Must match a key in ledger_scope_descriptions when provided.

treatment_type.description: Accounting treatment type for this leg
treatment_type.$comment: Must match one of the types in template's accounting_treatments array

condition.description: Reference to a boolean controlling conditional execution
condition.$comment: If the referenced value evaluates to false, the leg is skipped

legs.description: Transfer legs that generate the actual ledger transfers
legs.$comment: All leg fields reference variables or whitelisted selectors, keeping business logic in variables while allowing direct context access.

metadata_schema.description: JSON Schema for validating event's extra_metadata field
metadata_schema.$comment: Must be a valid JSON Schema document (2020-12 or later recommended)

description.description: Human-readable description of the example scenario

expected_transfers.description: Expected transfers that should be generated for validation

examples.description: Example scenarios for testing and documentation
examples.$comment: LIVE templates MUST have valid examples that pass all validations

examples.name: Retail GBP/EUR Exchange
examples.description: Exchanges a customer's money between their own GBP and EUR accounts at Northstar UK at a quoted rate; Northstar FX takes the other side through its vostros. Standard and Plus plans pay a fair-usage fee above their monthly allowance, at a rate set by the size of the exchange. The fee is FX income in the sold currency, booked by channel: app or partner app.
examples.trigger: Customer accepts a GBP/EUR exchange quote between two of their own accounts, in the Northstar app or in a partner app

account_code_validations.description: Customer's current account in the currency they sell
Customer's current account in the currency they buy
Northstar FX vostro at Northstar UK in the sold currency
Northstar FX vostro at Northstar UK in the bought currency
FX income of Northstar UK from in-app exchanges, GBP ledger
FX income of Northstar UK from in-app exchanges, EUR ledger
FX income of Northstar UK from partner-app exchanges, GBP ledger
FX income of Northstar UK from partner-app exchanges, EUR ledger

accounting_treatments.description: The customer's deposits are exchanged against Northstar FX's vostro balances at the quoted spot rate on the transaction date.
The fair-usage fee is revenue at the point in time the exchange is performed. It is booked by sales channel, app or partner app, so revenue can be disaggregated by channel.

financial_statements_impact.description: The customer's deposit falls by the amount sold plus any fee; Northstar FX's vostro rises by the amount sold.
FX income rises by the fair-usage fee when one is due.
Northstar FX's vostro falls and the customer's deposit rises by the same bought amount, so total liabilities on this ledger do not change.

ledger_scope_descriptions.operational_source: Northstar UK operational ledger in the currency the customer sells.
ledger_scope_descriptions.operational_target: Northstar UK operational ledger in the currency the customer buys.

variables.name: sell_currency
variables.description: Currency the customer sells. The fee is booked on this currency's ledger.

variables.name: buy_amount
variables.description: Amount the customer receives, in minor units of the bought currency, at the quoted rate.

variables.name: chargeable_amount
variables.description: Part of the sold amount above the plan's remaining fee-free allowance; zero on plans without the fee.

variables.name: fee_rate_bps
variables.description: Fee rate in basis points, by the size of the exchange: 0.5% below 5,000.00, 0.35% from 5,000.00, 0.25% from 25,000.00 of the sold currency.

variables.name: fx_fee
variables.description: Fair-usage fee in minor units of the sold currency, rounded half to even; zero when the event carries a fee waiver.

variables.name: via_partner_app
variables.description: True when a partner app started the exchange through the Northstar API.

variables.name: apply_fee_app_gbp
variables.description: A GBP fee is due on an exchange made in the Northstar app.

variables.name: apply_fee_app_eur
variables.description: A EUR fee is due on an exchange made in the Northstar app.

variables.name: apply_fee_partner_gbp
variables.description: A GBP fee is due on an exchange made in a partner app.

variables.name: apply_fee_partner_eur
variables.description: A EUR fee is due on an exchange made in a partner app.

variables.name: fx_fee_revenue_app_gbp
variables.description: FX trading income - GBP, UK: fees on exchanges made in the Northstar app.

variables.name: fx_fee_revenue_app_eur
variables.description: FX trading income - EUR, UK: fees on exchanges made in the Northstar app.

variables.name: fx_fee_revenue_partner_gbp
variables.description: FX trading income, partner apps - GBP, UK: fees on exchanges made in partner apps.

variables.name: fx_fee_revenue_partner_eur
variables.description: FX trading income, partner apps - EUR, UK: fees on exchanges made in partner apps.

validations.name: currencies_differ
validations.description: An exchange must sell one currency and buy another.

validations.name: customer_owns_both_accounts
validations.description: Customers exchange only between their own accounts.

validations.name: fx_hub_owns_both_vostros
validations.description: Both sides of the exchange sit with the same group entity.

validations.name: rate_quoted_for_this_pair
validations.description: The quoted rate must be for the currencies being exchanged, sold then bought.

validations.name: quote_still_valid
validations.description: The exchange must happen before the customer's quote expires.

legs.description: Customer sells the currency to Northstar FX at the quoted rate.
Northstar FX delivers the bought currency to the customer.
Charge the GBP fair-usage fee on an in-app exchange.
Charge the EUR fair-usage fee on an in-app exchange.
Charge the GBP fair-usage fee on a partner-app exchange.
Charge the EUR fair-usage fee on a partner-app exchange.

fx_rate.description: Quoted customer rate as a decimal string: units of the bought currency for one unit of the sold currency.

rate_pair.description: Currency pair of the quote as ISO 4217 codes, sold then bought. This template books fees on the GBP and EUR ledgers only.

quote_expires_at.description: Quote expiry in Unix milliseconds; the exchange must occur at or before it.

plan.description: Customer's account plan. Standard and Plus pay the fair-usage fee above their monthly allowance.

fee_free_allowance_remaining.description: Fee-free exchange allowance left this month, in minor units of the sold currency. Applies to Standard and Plus plans.

channel.description: Where the customer made the exchange: APP is the Northstar app; PARTNER_API is a partner app through the Northstar API. Sets the income account for the fee.

fee_waiver_reason.description: Why the fee is waived. Present only on a waived exchange, which books no fee.

quote_id.description: Identifier of the exchange quote the customer accepted.

examples.name: Standard plan in the app: GBP to EUR
examples.description: Sells GBP 1,000.00 at 1.1650 for EUR 1,165.00. GBP 400.00 of allowance is left, so the 0.5% fee applies to GBP 600.00: GBP 3.00, booked as app FX income.

examples.name: Standard plan in the app: EUR to GBP
examples.description: Sells EUR 500.00 at 0.8580 for GBP 429.00. No allowance is left, so the 0.5% fee applies to the whole amount: EUR 2.50, booked on the EUR ledger.

examples.name: Plus plan in a partner app: GBP 12,000 to EUR
examples.description: Sells GBP 12,000.00 at 1.1650 for EUR 13,980.00. The 0.35% rate applies from 5,000.00. GBP 1,000.00 of allowance is left, so the fee is GBP 38.50, booked as partner-app FX income.

examples.name: Standard plan in a partner app: EUR 30,000 to GBP
examples.description: Sells EUR 30,000.00 at 0.8580 for GBP 25,740.00. The 0.25% rate applies from 25,000.00, so the fee is EUR 75.00, booked as partner-app FX income on the EUR ledger.

examples.name: Premium plan, no fee: GBP to EUR
examples.description: Sells GBP 2,500.00 at 1.1650 for EUR 2,912.50. Premium pays no fair-usage fee, so no fee leg runs.

examples.name: Standard plan with a waived fee: GBP to EUR
examples.description: Sells GBP 800.00 at 1.1650 for EUR 932.00. The fee would be GBP 4.00, but the event carries a promotion waiver, so no fee leg runs.
